# Gyblos Explorer

> Live, public metrics of the Gyblos peer-to-peer AI inference network on Solana: which sellers are online, which models they serve and at what price, their uptime, how many requests the network served, and what Gyblos payment channels settled on chain.

Gyblos is an open market where anyone can sell, buy or give away AI inference. The explorer at https://explorer.gyblos.com shows the network as it is, from public sources only. It is on Solana devnet during the beta; mainnet is planned for 2026-12-09.

## How to read the figures

- Free and paid usage are always shown apart and never added together: cards label each number "free" or "paid", and tables give each figure a Free and a Paid column under one heading. Free volume is not backed by payment. Section titles name their range ("Usage, last 30 days").
- Usage comes from signed receipts that sellers and buyers report to the metrics collector. The request count includes requests only the seller reported; requests both sides reported are matched first.
- Buyer counts below 5 are withheld and shown as "< 5", never as zero.
- The Buyers card (Overview and Stats) counts distinct buyers of all time, free by NodeId and paid by wallet, never added, plus the ones new in the section's range; both up to the end of yesterday, UTC.
- Amounts are USDC, computed from exact atomic units. Times are UTC.
- Pages: `/` (Network) opens with an Overview of the range (sellers online, free and paid requests, distinct buyers of all time with the new ones in the range, USDC paid to sellers, average 24 h uptime), then the first Sellers page and the latest channel transactions; `/sellers` lists every seller online and not online; `/models` the models offered now and served over the range; `/transactions` every channel transaction; `/stats` usage and payments over the range, with their daily tables and unserved demand. The navigation also links to the docs. A seller counts as online when the index lists it, so the Overview count, the Sellers table and Not online agree. A change against the previous period is shown only when that period had activity; zero amounts read grey, and green marks USDC that moved.
- "Gyblos" channel figures come from payment channels whose opening transaction carries a Gyblos memo. That label is self-declared by whoever opens the channel.
- A ✓ next to a seller means the discovery index checked that the named GitHub account published the seller's NodeId in a gist; it links the seller to that account, does not identify a person and says nothing about quality. Sellers without it are not marked. A seller's self-chosen display name, when it set one, appears in smaller type below its account or NodeId in the Sellers and Not online tables (the account and its ✓ come first); it is not verified, and the ✓ belongs to the GitHub account, never to the name. Names carrying @, a check mark or hidden characters are not shown. Online sellers with at least 7 days of history come first, by whole-percent 7-day uptime and then by lowest paid output price; newer sellers follow, by price. `?verified=1` shows only verified sellers, online or not. What the check marks, names and amounts mean: https://docs.gyblos.com/en/reference/explorer
- A seller is online when it has a live signed presence in the discovery index, offline when it was seen before but has none now, and not published when it was never seen or withdrew its catalog.
- Channel transactions list the latest instructions of Gyblos payment channels on chain (channels whose open carries a Gyblos memo or whose distribute pays the Gyblos treasury), all time and newest first, not filtered by the range; `?before=<cursor>` pages to older ones. The Amount column is per row (the buyer deposit, newly settled, what the seller side received, or what went back to the buyer) and must not be added up; only Paid out is shown as money (green), other rows and batch totals are muted; a payout row also fills the rest of its split in its own USDC columns: Gyblos fee, Program (the payment program's own treasury: rounding remainders, or a share it could not deliver; not a Gyblos fee) and To buyer, and a note under the amount gives any unclassified remainder (and, on a refund row whose transaction also paid sellers, what went to sellers); a split shared by several channels is the transaction's batch total, shown on its first paying row, and the transaction's other paying rows say they are part of that payout. When the metrics collector does not send the split (an older collector), payout rows show no amount rather than the whole vault outflow. The seller is shown when the channel's payout recipient equals the owner address of exactly one listed seller; that owner is self-declared, so it is a display hint, not proof. A listed seller links to its page; a payout shared by several channels says "Several channels"; otherwise the row says "Unlisted seller".
- Each seller has a page at `/sellers/<NodeId>` (64 lowercase hex characters; anything else is a 404, and so is a NodeId that a whole, current read of the index does not know and that the collector has no activity for in the last 90 days; with a source down or dated, the page renders and is not indexed): its identicon, self-chosen name (not verified) when it set one, verified GitHub account, NodeId and self-declared owner address; its online, offline or not-published state with its online-since or last-seen time (and the time of the index read when it is dated), 24 h and 7 d uptime (only while it is listed); its requests, success rate, output tokens and seller first-token p50 over the range (free and paid apart), the paid usage both sides authorized, how many models it served ("100+" at the collector's cap of 100 models), free and paid requests-per-day charts, a model table (context and prices of its current offer; requests, success and first-token p50 over the range) and a daily table with buyer counts (below 5 shown as "< 5"); and the channel transactions whose payout recipient is its owner address, all time, newest first, with the same amount columns and colours as the main list (a batch total when a transaction paid several channels, which may include other sellers' channels). The owner address is published only while the seller is online, so an offline seller's page lists no transactions. There is no earned total: the collector has no per-seller on-chain total yet. Its tables use the same parameters as the Models, Stats and Transactions pages (`modelsPage`, `dailyPage`, `before` with `txPage`), and a link to a seller page keeps only `range` and `verified`.
- Each section that covers a span of days has its own 7, 30 or 90 day control and parameter: Overview (`overviewRange`), Models (`modelsRange`), Usage (`usageRange`), Payments (`paymentsRange`) and a seller page's Activity (`activityRange`); 30 is the default. An older `range` link sets the default for every section.
- Every table shows 5 rows per page, with its page in its own parameter: `sellersPage` (Sellers, after the verified filter and ordering), `offlinePage` (Not online), `modelsPage` (Models), `dailyPage` (Usage daily), `demandPage` (Unserved demand), `chainDailyPage` (Daily on chain) and `txPage` (Channel transactions, numbered alongside its `before` cursor). A missing, invalid or out-of-range page is dropped from the URL and shows page 1 (while a table's source answers only in part, an out-of-range page shows page 1 but stays in the URL), and every page link keeps the other parameters. Sortable columns carry a chevron; a click sorts highest first, then lowest first, then back to the default order (the day columns and Unserved demand start lowest first, since their default is already newest or most first), in the table's own parameter (`sellersSort`, `offlineSort`, `modelsSort`, `dailySort`, `demandSort`, `chainDailySort`; a leading `-` means highest first), and returns that table to page 1. A section's range switch returns only that section's tables to page 1 (Models; Usage daily and Unserved demand; Daily on chain); the other tables keep their page.
- Each seller links to its own page at `/sellers/<NodeId>`; the ✓ links to the GitHub proof gist.

## Public data sources

- [Discovery index](https://discovery.gyblos.com/v1/models): models offered now; `/v1/sellers?model=<id>` lists live sellers, `/v1/uptime?node=<NodeId>` a seller's uptime, and `/v1/network` every registered seller's online, offline or not-published state.
- [Metrics collector](https://collector.gyblos.com/v1/stats/network): daily network totals and `buyerTotals` (distinct buyers, all time and new in the range); `/v1/stats/models` per model and `/v1/stats/chain` on-chain settlements. Each takes `from` and `to` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, at most 92 days. `/v1/stats/sellers/<NodeId>` one seller's daily and per-model totals. `/v1/stats/chain/txs` lists Gyblos channel transactions, newest first, paged with `before` and `limit`, and `recipient=<address>` keeps only channels whose first payout recipient is that address (a payout's split then sits on the first matching row, with the whole transaction's values).
